 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the L.R's of one deceased Y.Sridhar Acharya S/o Y.Somaiah Acharya under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- in respect of his death in Road Traffic Accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 04.10.2023 at 5.45 am while Sridhar Acharya along with his wife Shuba, was traveling in car bearing no.KA-04-MJ-0726 from Mangalore to Bengaluru, when they reached opposite to Sriram Auto Mall near Kandalli village, Bengaluru-Mangalore-75, one Maruthi Breeza Car bearing no.KA-02-MU-0929 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed to the car of Sridhar Acharya and caused accident.
Due to the impact, himself and his wife sustained grievous injuries and they were taken to Jayachamarajendra hospital, Hassan for treatment.
When he (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.5047/2024 was under treatment on 04.10.2023 at 7.58 am, he died due to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Then post mortem was conducted and body was handed over to the petitioners.

The accident is caused due to sole negligence of driver of car bearing no.KA-02-MU-0929.
3.
Before accident deceased was running goldsmith shop in the name of Mangalore Sudarshan Jewellery Works at Krishna temple road, Bengaluru.
He was doing goldsmith work and earning sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month, contributing his entire towards his family.
Petitioners lost their earning member of the family, love and affection of husband and father respectively.

Hassan Traffic police have registered Crime No.209/2023 against the car driver for the offence p/u/s 279, 337, 338,
304(A) of IPC.

Petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.50,000/-
towards transportation of dead body.
4. 1st respondent is owner of car and 2nd respondent is insurance company which has issued policy in favour of aforesaid car which was valid as on the date of accident.
Therefore, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with costs and interest in the above case.
5. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 and 2 is served.
They appeared before this court through their respective counsel.
Both of them filed written statement.
1st respondent owner of the car bearing no.KA-02-MU- 0929 contended that the petition is not maintainable.
The age, occupation, income and permanent dependency alleged by the petitioners are denied.
Negligence on part of driver of said car is denied and contended that, he is the owner of the car and there is valid policy existing as on the date of accident covering from 29.06.2023 to 28.06.2024.
Further the driver had valid driving licence commencing from 08.07.2011 to 07.07.2031.
Therefore, if court comes to the conclusion of granting compensation, 2 nd respondent Shubha Sridhara Acharya vs Manjunath N on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47150844/

 (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.5047/2024  ISSUES 1.

No.KA-02-MU-0929 driven by its driver from behind in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-MJ-0726.
Due to which Y.Shreedhar Acharya sustained grievous injuries and died as alleged?

4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 (SCCH-12) 6 MVC.No.5047/2024  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative,

 REASONS 12. ISSUE NO.1: Petitioners, to prove that they are L.Rs of Sridhar Acharaya have not produced their I.D cards, but 1 st petitioner has produced passport of herself and her husband.
She has also produced D.L.
She has also produced birth certificate of her son and D.L of her husband.
They show that they are one family members.

The deceased is husband,
petitioner no.1 is wife, petitioner no.2 and 3 are their major children.
The relationship is not seriously in dispute.
Therefore, petitioners have proved that they are L.Rs of Sridhar Acharya and competent persons to file this petition.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE No.2:
According to petitioners the driver of opponent car was negligent in driving the vehicle.
To prove the same, P.W.1 in her chief examination affidavit stated about the negligence of opponent car driver.
She relied upon the FIR, spot panchanama, vehicle accident report, inquest report, postmortem report and final report in that regard.
14. On perusal of those documents it can be seen that, Sudarshan Acharya i.e., 2nd petitioner is first informant.
(SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.5047/2024 Information is given to police on the same day of the accident.
The spot of accident is national highway.

In the first information it is stated petitioner no.1 and her husband were going in Maruti Alto car on 03.10.2023 and on the NH 75 the opponent car came in rash and negligent manner and hit the alto car of the petitioner.
That parents of this first informant were sent to hospital but his father died due to accidental injuries.
He prayed to take action against the opponent cr driver by mentioning car registration number.
15. Spot panchanama was conducted and sketch is drawn.
It shows there was road repair on highway and one side vehicular movements were diverted to other side of the road.
Hence the one way was converted to two way road to allow vehicular movements of both sides.
Accident took place on the left side of Managalore Bengalore road, which shows driver of the opponent car came to right side of the road and hit the car coming on left side.
The said negligence on his part is simply denied in his written statement.
But no supporting evidence is given both by 1st and 2nd respondents.

The opponent driver also sustained injury in the accident and even his carmates have sustained injuries Shubha Sridhara Acharya vs Manjunath N on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47150844/

16. PW1 is not only LR of the deceased but she is victim as well as eye witness to the accident.
She denied negligence on her husband's part in driving the vehicle.
No contrary evidence is placed against her evidence by the respondent side.
Hence on (SCCH-12) 8 MVC.No.5047/2024 the basis of oral and documentary evidence, petitioners have proved the negligence on part of opponent car driver in driving the vehicle.
Hence this issue is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.3: Respondents disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
To prove the age of the deceased petitioners mentioned in the petition that deceased was aged 63 years at the time of accident.
They have produced D.L of the deceased at Ex.P.10.
It shows he was born on 23.09.1959.
As on the date of accident deceased was aged 63 years.
Therefore it is considered that the was aged about 63 years at the time of accident.
18. In the petition it is mentioned that deceased was doing Goldsmith work and earning Rs.1,00,000/-per month.
To prove his occupation some gold smith receipts and book maintained by him are produced.
His account statement or business IT returns are not produced.
As such alleged income of Rs. 1 lakh per month is not proved.
Hence, notional income has to be considered.
Accident being taken place in 2023, considering cost of living, his income per month is considered as Rs.16,000/-.
In the petition it is stated that all the petitioners were dependents upon the deceased.
They are wife and two major sons among whom 2nd petitioner is working in Dell Company and 2nd son is still studying.
1st petitioner is also said to be working.
But their separate income is not proved.
Hence, all of them are considered as dependents on the deceased.
Hence this issue is answered in the Partly in the Affirmative.
(SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.5047/2024 19. ISSUE No.4:
In view of above reasons, petitioners are entitled for compensation for the negligence of opponent car driver.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under;
20. Loss of dependency :
As per the Praney Sethi case future prospects of the deceased will have to be added to the monthly income.
In this case age of deceased is 63.
Hence, no future prospect has to be added.
As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.13,44,000/-

sentences.text: Loss of love and affection:
Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their husband and father respectively due to his death in the accident.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
22. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.5047/2024 Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/-
respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident being taken place in the year 2023, under the head of loss of estate Rs.16,500/-, for funeral expenses Rs.16,500/- and for loss of consortium Rs.44,000/- each to petitioner No. 1 to 3 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:
Sl. Particulars of Heads Amount in Rs.
No.
1. Loss of Dependency : Rs. 13,44,000-00 2. Loss of love & affection : Rs. 50,000-00 3. Loss of Consortium to : Rs. 1,32,000-00  petitioner No. 1 to 3  ( Rs.44,000/- each)
4. Loss of estate : Rs. 16,500-00 5.
Funeral expenses : Rs. 16,500-00  TOTAL Rs. 15,59,000-00
Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.15,59,000/-.
In view of valid insurance policy existing as on the date of accident to the opponent car, 2nd respondent insurance company is liable to pay compensation to petitioners.
Hence, I answer this Issue in "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. ISSUE No.5:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- in respect of death of Sridhara Acharya in road traffic accident.
They have not claimed any rate of interest on the compensation amount.
But as per the settled law, the (SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.5047/2024 interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
They being L.rs of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 70:15:15.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

22. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Praney Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.5047/2024 Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/-
respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident being taken place in the year 2023, under the head of loss of estate Rs.16,500/-, for funeral expenses Rs.16,500/- and for loss of consortium Rs.44,000/- each to petitioner No. 1 to 3 is awarded.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation as under:

Therefore, I hold that the petitioners are entitled for a compensation of Rs.15,59,000/-.
23. ISSUE No.5:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- in respect of death of Sridhara Acharya in road traffic accident.
They have not claimed any rate of interest on the compensation amount.
But as per the settled law, the (SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.5047/2024 interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.
They being L.rs of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 70:15:15.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,59,000/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.

In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.2 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 2 months from the date of this order.
Out of the total compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioners, they are entitled to the compensation in the apportionment of 70:15:15.

In such apportionment entire compensation awarded to petitioner no.2 and 3 shall be released in their favour without making F.D (SCCH-12) 12 MVC.No.5047/2024 and 50% of compensation awarded to 1 st petitioner wife of the deceased shall be kept in F.D in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be released in her favour.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
